newRules.title: Supabase authorization traps
newRules.text: No policy or function authorizes from `user_metadata` / `raw_user_meta_data` (users can edit it, and it appears in `auth.jwt()`); every UPDATE policy has both `USING` and `WITH CHECK`; `TO authenticated` is always paired with an ownership predicate (alone it is authentication, not authorization); `SECURITY DEFINER` functions live outside exposed schemas or have `EXECUTE` revoked from `PUBLIC` and `anon`; the CLI, CI, MCP servers and agents use scoped personal access tokens, never a full-account token; deleting a user revokes their sessions first (access tokens outlive the user). *Test:* a migration lint for `user_metadata` and for UPDATE policies without `WITH CHECK`; pgTAP for cross-user update and post-deletion access.
newRules.modeReason: security floor ("authoriz") — never relaxed in quick mode

notes: Vendor skill (MIT), prompt-only. Could also be pinned as a companion later; distilled so the facts have one owner.
rationale: Vendor source, so its Supabase facts are authoritative (user_metadata is user-editable, UPDATE needs WITH CHECK, scoped tokens, sessions outlive deleted users). Distilled into SUPA-5 rather than pinned, so the facts have one owner beside SUPA-1…4.
